about: Reference pack for the hydrofoil moth (docs/moth-1). Photos of real foiling moths for looking and measuring proportions only: nothing is traced into the model, no photo enters the repo, and no builder's name, logo or sail graphics are copied (several photos show them; the game's boat is an invented design with an invented class name). Public domain, CC0 or plain CC BY only (no NC, ND or SA), as for the C22, the J-Class, the frigate and the Hobie 16. Download with python3 -I Tools/shipkit/fetch_refs.py Tools/shipkit/moth/refs.json Data/Reference/raw/boats/Moth (git-ignored; fetch_refs.py reads each file's licence on Commons first and refuses anything else).
status: Nov 25 2026: Commons' Category:Moth (dinghy) holds 39 files, read through the desktop app's browser (licences and authors from Commons' own metadata). 13 are CC BY-SA (left out, among them the only view from below, 'Moth unten Kiel2008.jpg'), one is an svg emblem, several are distant or show the 1987 low-riding boat. These are the usable ones. 'viewed_nov25' marks the ones looked at in slice 0 (the cloud's downloads got rate-limited after eight).

drawings.use: slices 1, 3, 4: THE flying broadside, nearly square on: ride height (hull bottom over the water), main strut and rudder lengths, the gantry, the wand trailing from the bow, mast and boom height. Read on Nov 25: the hull flies about a strut's half-length clear

slices 2-3: a boat laid on its side on the bank, foils in the air: the main strut and T-foil, the rudder on its gantry with its elevator, the wand and its pivot at the bow, the wing bars and the hull's underside
slice 1: the hull afloat with her sailor before take-off: the static waterline, freeboard and how low the narrow hull floats; the wings' height over the water
slices 3-4 and the physics: lifting off, the hull just clearing the water, the rig tipped to windward
physics: flying heeled to windward, the sailor hiked off the wing, a moment before a crash (the photographer's caption); the strut and rudder in the water at speed
slice 3: flying ('And flying!', not yet viewed)

drawings.use: slices 1, 4: two current boats ashore on trolleys, broadside: the hull's profile and deck, the deck-sweeper sail's foot, the wings from the side, a person for scale
slices 2-4: flying from the bow quarter: the wings' outline, both foils in the water, the boom and battens. Carries a builder's logos and sail graphics: look only, never copied
slice 3: flying on her foils (not yet viewed; small)
